falseSynonyms.zh: train = structured development practise = repeat a particular skill Compare: - She trains for tennis tournaments. - She practises her serve every morning.
falseSynonyms.point: train = structured development practise = repeat a particular skill Compare: - She trains for tennis tournaments. - She practises her serve every morning.

falseSynonyms.zh: train is one possible method of preparation. prepare is broader. Compare: - He trained for the marathon. - He prepared for the marathon by training, eating carefully, and resting.
falseSynonyms.point: train is one possible method of preparation. prepare is broader. Compare: - He trained for the marathon. - He prepared for the marathon by training, eating carefully, and resting.

falseSynonyms.zh: teach often focuses on knowledge or understanding. train often focuses on practical performance. Compare: - teach mathematics - train someone to operate machinery There is overlap, but the typical contexts differ.
falseSynonyms.point: teach often focuses on knowledge or understanding. train often focuses on practical performance. Compare: - teach mathematics - train someone to operate machinery There is overlap, but the typical contexts differ.

falseSynonyms.zh: coach usually includes feedback on performance. Compare: - train new employees - coach an athlete on technique
falseSynonyms.point: coach usually includes feedback on performance. Compare: - train new employees - coach an athlete on technique

falseSynonyms.zh: exercise = physical activity for health or fitness train = purposeful preparation for performance Compare: - I exercise to stay healthy. - I train for competitive cycling.
falseSynonyms.point: exercise = physical activity for health or fitness train = purposeful preparation for performance Compare: - I exercise to stay healthy. - I train for competitive cycling.

falseSynonyms.zh: practise is broad. rehearse is usually for a specific performance, speech, scene, or presentation. Compare: - practise pronunciation - rehearse a presentation
falseSynonyms.point: practise is broad. rehearse is usually for a specific performance, speech, scene, or presentation. Compare: - practise pronunciation - rehearse a presentation

falseSynonyms.zh: Both involve repetition. drill suggests: - stronger repetition - precision - automatic response Compare: - practise vocabulary - drill emergency procedures
falseSynonyms.point: Both involve repetition. drill suggests: - stronger repetition - precision - automatic response Compare: - practise vocabulary - drill emergency procedures

falseSynonyms.zh: educate develops understanding and knowledge. train develops practical competence. Compare: - educate the public about nutrition - train nurses to use new equipment
falseSynonyms.point: educate develops understanding and knowledge. train develops practical competence. Compare: - educate the public about nutrition - train nurses to use new equipment

falseSynonyms.zh: mentor involves long-term guidance and support. train focuses more directly on competence.
falseSynonyms.point: mentor involves long-term guidance and support. train focuses more directly on competence.

falseSynonyms.zh: groom means deliberately prepare someone for a future position. Example: - train a manager in budgeting - groom a manager for promotion
falseSynonyms.point: groom means deliberately prepare someone for a future position. Example: - train a manager in budgeting - groom a manager for promotion

falseSynonyms.zh: Knowing where the buttons are is not the same as being fully trained. familiarize = become acquainted train = develop competence
falseSynonyms.point: Knowing where the buttons are is not the same as being fully trained. familiarize = become acquainted train = develop competence

falseSynonyms.zh: These are close but not identical. undergo training emphasizes experiencing the full training process. attend training simply means being present at training sessions. Someone can attend a session without successfully completing the training.
falseSynonyms.point: These are close but not identical. undergo training emphasizes experiencing the full training process. attend training simply means being present at training sessions. Someone can attend a session without successfully completing the training.

falseSynonyms.zh: study often involves reading, learning, and academic effort. train often involves practical development. Compare: - study law - train as a lawyer
falseSynonyms.point: study often involves reading, learning, and academic effort. train often involves practical development. Compare: - study law - train as a lawyer

falseSynonyms.zh: learn describes gaining knowledge or skill. train describes a structured process used to develop it. Compare: - She learned CPR. - She trained in CPR. - train employees - train athletes - train recruits Example: The company trains new employees. - train staff to use the system - train dogs to respond to commands Example: Staff are trained to identify safety risks. - train for a marathon - train for a competition - train as a nurse - train as an engineer - train in first aid - train in conflict resolution - practise pronunciation - practise the piano - practise speaking - practise driving Not normally: - practise to speak ✗ Better: - practise speaking - prepare for an interview - prepare for an exam - prepare to leave - prepare to compete - prepare students for work - undergo safety training - undergo specialist training - undergo military training - coach athletes - coach students - coach someone in public speaking - coach someone on interview technique - instruct staff to evacuate - instruct recruits in first aid - rehearse a speech - rehearse the play - rehearse for the concert - familiarize staff with the procedure - familiarize yourself with the rules
